title: TM184C is a GPCR-like regulator of intercellular exchange and autophagy.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the Zenodo record (CC-BY-4.0): Dataset_S1.tsv 1.21 GB, Dataset_S2.xlsx 28.5 KB, Dataset_S3.xlsx 142 MB, Dataset_S4.xlsx 172 MB. Downloaded S2 in full: one sheet, 880 rows x 2 columns of AlphaFold model IDs listed as 'Foldseek pass' / 'Foldseek fail'. Range-read the first 20 KB of S1: columns rank, tm, coverage, type, protein, gene, protein_existence, superkingdom, organism, lineage, primary_accession, interpro_ids, source, status, id_line, sequence_aa; the first rows are rhodopsin homologues with TM-score (a structure-alignment similarity score) 0.95.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Total hit count (~1.46M; 506,129 GPCRs and 955,350 non-GPCR 7TMPs, meaning seven-transmembrane proteins) and the contents of S3/S4 (over the 50 MB cap, not opened). Cell-assay source data (beta-arrestin recruitment, autophagy, nanotube imaging) is attached to the Nature article and was not retrieved; Europe PMC's supplement endpoint timed out.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo, open, CC-BY-4.0; checked the file listing and downloaded S2 plus the first 20 KB of S1.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in S1: a TM-score column ('tm') and a rank column exist; the GPCR vs non-GPCR split is per the paper the S3/S4 file membership (not opened).

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: S1 carries full amino-acid sequences ('sequence_aa') and UniProt accessions.

a4_units_stated.note: TM-score is unitless on a 0-1 scale; rank is categorical (paper text).

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper says ~1.46M hits; I only saw the first ~21 rows of S1, so the count is unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: S1 is 1.21 GB (checked size); it can be streamed or subset by columns, but embedding over a million sequences on a CPU would take days.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without downloading the 1.2 GB S1; no contradiction seen.

a8_label_provenance.note: Every candidate label is computed, not measured: 'tm'/rank come from structural alignment of AlphaFold2 predicted models against GPCR templates, and the GPCR/non-GPCR class comes from UniProt/InterPro annotations, which also sit in S1's own 'interpro_ids' column (leakage by construction). The only measured labels, from cell assays, cover a handful of proteins.

existing_models.name: TM-Vec / TM-Vec 2 (predicts TM-score from sequence pairs with protein language model embeddings)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported TM-score error within 0.026 for remote homologues with <=10% sequence identity (Nature Biotechnology 2023); TM-Vec 2 is a faster distilled version (bioRxiv 2026).

existing_models.name: PLMSearch (protein language model remote-homology search trained on structural-similarity labels)
GPCR-SLM (small transformer classifying GPCRs into 86 families)
existing_models.score_and_split: 99% accuracy versus BLAST 86.1% and HMMER 91% (split not retrieved).

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model)
backbone.hardware: CPU for small checkpoints on a subset; the full ~1.46M sequences would be days of CPU time

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None that escapes circularity: the joinable resources are the same annotations and predicted structures the labels were derived from.

controls.positive_control: Recover known GPCR families (rhodopsin rank 1) from sequence alone.
controls.external_validation: None independent; GPCRdb would just restate the annotation labels.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here would only reproduce Foldseek/TM-align scores on AlphaFold2 models, or InterPro GPCR annotations, from sequence; it would make no claim about measured GPCR-like signalling.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence to predict how structurally similar a protein's predicted shape is to known G-protein-coupled receptors.
plain_idea.train_on: Amino-acid sequences of seven-transmembrane proteins mined from the AlphaFold structure database; the paper reports ~1.46M, unverified (I saw ~21 rows).
plain_idea.predict: The structural similarity score (TM-score) to receptor templates, or GPCR vs non-GPCR class; both are computed from predicted structures or database annotations, not measured in a lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Could flag 'dark' receptor-like proteins without folding them, but TM-Vec and PLMSearch already do this, and the labels are computed rather than measured.

ml_idea: Sequence-to-TM-score or sequence-to-GPCR-class regression or classification on S1 with ESM-2 embeddings. Rejected: the labels are AlphaFold-plus-alignment outputs or annotation-derived, and TM-Vec, PLMSearch and GPCR classifiers already cover the task.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project is rejected at A8.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Trace the label provenance: 'tm' comes from aligning AlphaFold2 models and the class from InterPro, both confirmed from the S1 header and the paper's methods.

verdict_reason: A8 fails. The deposited 1.2 GB table holds only computed labels: TM-scores from aligning AlphaFold2 predicted models, and GPCR classes from InterPro annotations that also appear as an S1 column. The measured cell-assay data covers only a few proteins, and sequence-to-TM-score is already handled by open models (TM-Vec, PLMSearch).
